escalation_reason: STABILIZED, NOT RESOLVED. mark_dlq_permanent executed successfully and list_dlq_messages confirmed it landed on 87f50f4d-ca7e-508e-9820-63c1a24c8f52 — this is an escalation by design, not a failed remediation. mark_dlq_permanent is a stabilize-only action: fences one dead-lettered job out of auto-replay — it sets `remediation_hint=human_required` and writes the operator's reason to the audit trail, and the platform's own description says it "doesn't change job.status — the entry stays in DLQ". So the job is still dead and its work is still undone: the fence stops a later bulk replay from re-running a poisoned payload, and it fixes nothing about why the payload failed. The bad data, the producer bug or the schema behind it is untouched and a human still has to act. Unlike a pause the fence does not expire, so nothing is on a clock — but 'permanent' describes the fence, not the incident. The underlying fault on 87f50f4d-ca7e-508e-9820-63c1a24c8f52 is unchanged and still needs a human decision on the real fix. Treat the stabilization as a clock, not an outcome.

findings: The chain's root job 87f50f4d-ca7e-508e-9820-63c1a24c8f52 (bulk_api_sync) is dead-lettered after exhausting its three retries, and the descendant behind it is still waiting. The upstream parent completed normally, so the failure is isolated to the root. Because dead_letter is terminal and the resolver only promotes a child whose parents have all completed, nothing will move this chain without intervention. The root's dead-letter row is classified human_required on "SchemaValidationError: payload missing required field 'user_id' (received keys: ['tenant_id', 'action', 'ts'])" — a value missing from the stored payload, not a platform fault, so every replay re-reads the same bytes and fails again. The root is now fenced with mark_dlq_permanent: stamped with fenced_at, excluded from any future category or bulk replay, still dead-lettered, chain still stuck. The four other rows in the queue (one replay_safe, two wait_and_replay, one already human_required) were left untouched — they are not this incident.
recommendation: Fix the producer, then replay the root by id: whatever emits this bulk_api_sync payload is dropping the required field 'user_id' — the row shows the payload arrived with only ['tenant_id', 'action', 'ts']. The fence stops auto-replay and nothing else, so the chain stays stuck until someone corrects the payload and replays 87f50f4d-ca7e-508e-9820-63c1a24c8f52 with replay_dlq_by_ids, which is the call that lets the resolver promote the waiting descendants. A fenced row is still replayable by explicit id, so the fence takes nothing away from that decision — it only keeps a bulk sweep from making it for you. Do not replay the root before the payload is fixed: it will fail identically and burn another attempt.
